test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which of the following years was Birsa Munda arrested by the Britishers, convicted on charges of rioting and jailed for two years?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1895**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Birsa Munda** was born at Ulhiatu in the erstwhile Bengal presidency, **now in the Khunti district of Jharkhand**.
 
• He was the son of **“Sugna Munda” and “Karmi Hatu”.**
 
• Due to extreme poverty, Birsa Munda left his ancestral village and went to his maternal uncle’s home at Ayubhatu where he lived for two years.
 
• Birsa Munda received his primary education in Salga which was run by Jaipal Nag, after that he was admitted to a German mission school where he adopted Christianity.
 
• **From 1886 to 90 Birsa’s family resided in Chaibasa and came under the influence of Sardar’s movement, Birsa left his German membership and joined the movement.**
 
• In the 1890s Birsa Munda started spreading awareness among the people about the laws against tribal people and to access total control of India.
 
• Birsa Munda revolted against the Britishers, especially against the laws which were against the agrarian structure of tribal people’s lands and their cultural identity.
 
• As the movement spread British officials decided to act.
 
• They **arrested Birsa in 1895**, convicted him** on charges of rioting and jailed him for two years.**
 
• In June** 1900, Birsa Munda died at the mere age of 25 years **while kept in Ranchi jail; he became a god-like figure among the tribal people of his state.
 
• A famous slogan of Birsa Munda was “Let the kingdom of King and Queen be ended and our kingdom is established” which was accepted by the whole nation.
